name: Huawei CloudMatrix 384 (CM384) supernode — 384x Ascend 910C
memory_bandwidth_basis: AGGREGATE SYSTEM FIGURE. 384 x 128 GB = 49,152 GB (48 TB) total HBM; 384 x 3.2 TB/s = 1,228.8 TB/s aggregate memory bandwidth. Per-NPU: 128 GB at 3.2 TB/s. Source: Huawei CloudMatrix384 engineering paper arXiv:2506.12708v1 (cited by flopper.io) and China Research Collective analysis.
notes: THE HIERARCHY POINT: CloudMatrix 384 is not a chip but a rack-scale system — 384 Ascend 910C NPUs across 16 racks (12 compute, 4 network) with 192 Kunpeng CPUs, connected via Huawei's Unified Bus (UB) for fully non-blocking all-to-all interconnect. This is Huawei's answer to the Ascend 910B's HCCS scale-up problem: instead of making the chip-to-chip fabric faster, they bought optical bandwidth at the system level. SYSTEM FIGURES (vendor-published, arXiv:2506.12708v1): ~300 PFLOPS BF16 dense, 48 TB HBM, 559 kW system power. The China Research Collective analysis (June 2026) gives slightly different figures: ~289 PFLOPS BF16, 48 TB HBM, 350-500 kW. The discrepancy is likely measurement vs. theoretical peak. UB INTERCONNECT: 196 GB/s unidirectional per NPU (7 x 224 Gbps transceivers per NPU), with L1 on-board switching (7 UB Switch chips per node) and L2 rack-level switching (112 L2 UB switch chips across 4 communication racks). Scale-out is 200 Gbps RoCE RDMA per NPU (76.8 Tbps total). The system uses 6,912 800G LPO optical transceivers for entirely optical intra- and inter-rack connectivity. DEEPSEEK V4 PRO INFERENCE: 6,688 tokens/s/NPU prefill, 1,943 tokens/s/NPU decode — reportedly exceeding H100/H800 under the same conditions. At TPOT < 50 ms, CM384 maintains 538 tokens/s/NPU while H100/H800 drop to 30-40% of peak. The 128 GB HBM per NPU (60% more than H100/H800's 80 GB) allows larger models or longer context. Vendor is 'asic-other' because 'huawei' is not in the schema enum; the real vendor is Huawei HiSilicon.
